# Split series of a group generated by a split normal subgroup and a split group

This derived unit proves a splitness criterion over a field `k`. Let `P` be a smooth
affine group over `Spec k`, and let `N ⟶ P` be a smooth, connected, normal, closed
subgroup that is split unipotent. Let `H` be a smooth, connected, affine group with a
split series, and let `i : H ⟶ P` be a homomorphism. If the morphism
`(n, h) ↦ j n * i h` from `N × H` onto `P` is surjective, then `P` is split unipotent,
in the sense of the published `RelativeRoot.IsSplitUnipotent`.

The proof needs closed images of homomorphisms, and the Library does not yet provide
them. This unit therefore takes them as the explicit hypothesis `HomImageHypothesis k`
described below, and does not prove that hypothesis. The unit changes no published
definition.

Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), §16.g "Split solvable groups", printed p.343 (PDF
p.359), says: "Quotients of split solvable groups are split because nontrivial quotients
of Ga and Gm are isomorphic to Ga or Gm (Exercise 14-3). Extensions of split solvable
groups are obviously split". For a group `P = N·H` with `N` normal, the remark gives
splitness of `P`: `P/N` is a quotient of `H`, and `P` is an extension of `P/N` by `N`.
The Lean proof does not form `P/N` as a quotient of `H`. It runs an induction on the
series of `H` inside `P`, described below, and uses the published Ga-quotient lemma
(`trivial_or_isVectorGroup_of_flat_surjective`) and the extension lemma
(`HasSplitSeries.of_fppfQuotient_of_field`).

## Definitions

- `mulPoints j i : N.X ⊗ H.X ⟶ P.X`, for homomorphisms `j : N ⟶ P` and `i : H ⟶ P` over
  any base scheme, is the morphism `(fst ≫ j) * (snd ≫ i)`. On points it sends `(n, h)`
  to `j n * i h`. `mulPoints_eq_mulMap` records that, when `range j` is normal and `j`
  is a monomorphism, `mulPoints j i` is by definition the published multiplication
  morphism `Semidirect.mulMap` of the semidirect product `N ⋊ H`.
- `HomImageHypothesis k` is a proposition, an interface for images that this unit
  assumes and does not prove. It says: for every homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ G` of group
  schemes over `Spec k`, with `A` smooth, connected and affine and `G` smooth and
  affine, there are a closed subgroup `inc : D ⟶ G` and a homomorphism `fac : A ⟶ D`
  with `fac ≫ inc = φ`. Here `fac` is flat, surjective and quasi-compact, and `D` is
  smooth, connected and affine. `D` is the image of `φ`. For algebraic groups over a
  field, Milne's homomorphism theorem (Theorem 5.39, printed p.108, PDF p.124) gives
  such a factorization `φ = i ∘ q` with `q` faithfully flat and `i` a closed immersion.

## Helpers

- `isMonHom_of_comp_eq`: let `inc : D ⟶ G` be a homomorphism that is a monomorphism, and
  let `g : X ⟶ D.X` be a morphism such that `g ≫ inc` is a homomorphism. Then `g` is a
  homomorphism. This is checked on points after cancelling `inc`.
- `mem_range_of_comp_mem`: let `inc : D ⟶ G` be a homomorphism whose underlying scheme
  morphism is a monomorphism, and let `π : T' ⟶ T` be a morphism of tests that is flat,
  surjective and quasi-compact. Suppose a point `c` of `G` on `T` has `π ≫ c` in the
  range of `inc`, say `π ≫ c = y ≫ inc`. Then `c` is in the range of `inc`. The proof
  descends `y` along the effective epimorphism `π` (Mathlib's fpqc instance). The
  descent condition holds because `inc` is a monomorphism, and the descended map
  factors `c` because `π` is an epimorphism.
- `comp_eq_one_of_mem`: if the kernel of `π : G ⟶ Q` has the same range as `inc`, then
  `(z ≫ inc) ≫ π = 1` for every point `z` of `D`.
- `isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective`: the target of a flat surjective morphism of schemes
  from a reduced scheme is reduced. Every stalk map is a flat local homomorphism, hence
  faithfully flat and injective (Mathlib's
  `Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom`). So the stalks of the target are
  reduced.
- `conj_mem_of`: in a group, if `a`, `b c b⁻¹` and `b d b⁻¹` lie in a subgroup `R`, then
  so does `(a b) (c d) (a b)⁻¹`.

## Main theorem

`isSplitUnipotent_of_surjective (hIm : HomImageHypothesis k) (n : ℕ)`: for all `P`, `N`
and `H` over `Spec k` with `P` smooth and affine, `N` smooth and connected, `H` smooth,
connected and affine, all homomorphisms `j : N ⟶ P` and `i : H ⟶ P`, a closed subgroup
`j` with normal range, `IsSplitUnipotent N`, `HasSplitSeries n H`, and a surjective
`(mulPoints j i).left`, the group `P` satisfies `IsSplitUnipotent P`. The proof is by
induction on `n`, for all `P`, `N`, `H`, `j` and `i` at once. The length of the
resulting series of `P` is not tracked, because trivial Ga steps may disappear.

**Base case.** If `H` has the series of length zero, every point of `H` is `1`, so
`mulPoints j i = fst ≫ j`. Thus `j` is surjective. A surjective closed immersion into
the reduced scheme `P` (smooth over a field: `isReduced_of_smooth_over_field`) is an
isomorphism (Mathlib's `isIso_of_isClosedImmersion_of_surjective`). So `range j` is all
of `P`. Then `IsClosedSubgroup.sourceIsoOfRangeEq` gives `N ≅ P`, and
`HasSplitSeries.of_iso` transports the series of `N`.

**Inductive step.** The series of `H` gives a closed, normal, smooth, connected subgroup
`jK : K ⟶ H`, with a series of length `n`, and an fppf quotient `qK : H ⟶ V` with
kernel `K` and `V` a one-dimensional vector group.

1. *The image `D` of `N ⋊ K`.* Normality of `range j` makes `range j` stable under
   conjugation by `jK ≫ i`. The published semidirect product `A = N ⋊ K` is smooth,
   affine and connected: its underlying scheme is the fibre product `N ×_k K`, and `N`
   is geometrically connected by the Library's `geometricallyConnected_of_connected`.
   `hIm` applied to `Semidirect.mulHom : A ⟶ P` gives the closed subgroup
   `inc : D ⟶ P` and the flat, surjective, quasi-compact `fac : A ⟶ D`.
2. *`N` and `K` inside `D`.* `j' = inl ≫ fac` and `i' = inr ≫ fac` satisfy
   `j' ≫ inc = j` and `i' ≫ inc = jK ≫ i`. They are homomorphisms by
   `isMonHom_of_comp_eq`. `j'` is a closed immersion by Mathlib's cancellation
   `IsClosedImmersion.of_comp_isClosedImmersion`. `range j'` is normal in `D` because
   `range j` is normal in `P` and `inc` is a monomorphism. Cancelling `inc` shows
   `mulPoints j' i' = fac`, which is surjective. The induction hypothesis applied to
   `(D, N, K, j', i')` gives a series of some length `r` for `D`.
3. *`D` is normal in `P`.* The morphism `mulPoints j i` is flat by the published
   `DominantHomFlat.flat_of_isDominant`. It is surjective, of finite type and
   quasi-compact (its source is affine and `P` is separated), and its target `P` is
   reduced and locally noetherian. So the product
   `mulPoints j i ⊗ fac : (N × H) × A ⟶ P × D` is flat, surjective and quasi-compact.
   Write `c = fst * (snd ≫ inc) * fst⁻¹ : P × D ⟶ P` for the conjugation morphism.
   Composed with this cover, `c` becomes `(j n · i h)(j n₁ · i jK k₁)(j n · i h)⁻¹`.
   This lies in the range of `inc` by `conj_mem_of`: `range j` is normal in `P` and
   lies in the range of `inc`, and `h · jK k₁ · h⁻¹ = jK k₂` because `range jK` is normal
   in `H`. `mem_range_of_comp_mem` then puts `c` in the range of `inc`. Normality on
   any test follows by composing `c` with `lift g y`.
4. *The quotient `Q = P / D`.* The published `smoothSubgroupQuotientExistence` gives a
   separated, locally finite-type quotient scheme with a smooth, surjective,
   quasi-compact projection with fibres the `D`-cosets. The published
   `NormalQuotient.groupScheme`, `NormalQuotient.hom` and
   `NormalQuotient.isFppfQuotient` make it a group `Q` with fppf quotient `πQ : P ⟶ Q`
   whose kernel has the range of `inc`.
5. *The map `ψ : V ⟶ Q`.* Points of the kernel of `qK` lie in `range jK`, and
   `jK ≫ i = i' ≫ inc` is killed by `πQ`. So `i ≫ πQ` kills the kernel of `qK`. `qK`
   is flat, surjective and quasi-compact (its source is affine and `V` is affine by the
   published `AdditiveGroupQuotient.isAffine`). The published homomorphism descent
   `FpqcHomDescent.hom` then gives `ψ : V ⟶ Q` with `qK ≫ ψ = i ≫ πQ`. Since
   `j ≫ πQ = 1`, `mulPoints j i ≫ πQ = snd ≫ qK ≫ ψ`, so `ψ` is surjective. `Q` is
   reduced by `isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective` and locally noetherian (of finite type
   over `k`), and `ψ` is of finite type and quasi-compact (`V` is isomorphic to the
   affine line by the published `AdditiveGroupQuotient.lineIso`). So `ψ` is flat by
   `DominantHomFlat.flat_of_isDominant`.
6. *Conclusion.* The published `trivial_or_isVectorGroup_of_flat_surjective` gives
   `HasSplitSeries 0 Q` or `IsVectorGroupOfDimension Q 1`. In the first case the
   published extension lemma `HasSplitSeries.of_fppfQuotient_of_field` (with `D` as
   kernel) gives `HasSplitSeries (r + 0) P`. In the second case the data
   `(D, Q, inc, πQ)` is directly a witness of `HasSplitSeries (r + 1) P`: `inc` is a
   closed subgroup, `D` is smooth and connected, `range inc` is normal, `πQ` is an fppf
   quotient with kernel `range inc`, `Q` is a one-dimensional vector group and `D` has
   the series of length `r`.

## Provenance

The unit is derived. Its conclusion is a case of Milne's remark that, in the group
`N·H`, quotients and extensions of split groups are split. The route is internal to
this formalization: induction on the series of `H` through the images of `N ⋊ K`,
normality by fpqc descent of membership, and the descended map `V ⟶ P/D`.
`mulPoints` and `HomImageHypothesis` are auxiliary definitions for this proof.
`HomImageHypothesis` is a hypothesis of the main theorem and is not proved here.

The reducedness-descent helper reuses the identical published proposition
in `AlgebraicGeometry/GeometricallyReducedOfAlgClosedProof`.
